Definition for this course: Structured sales process connecting use case discovery, workflow/value evidence and executive alignment to a validation decision.
Boundary / example: Not a guaranteed pilot or post-sales reference architecture.

Definition for this course: Outcome-led discovery and prioritization of candidate use cases.
Boundary / example: First customer-facing step; duration varies by source/context.

Definition for this course: Detailed investigation of a prioritized workflow with practitioners and business/technical owners.
Boundary / example: Current work, future hypothesis, time, systems and business consequence.

Definition for this course: Optional review of mapped workflows or targeted future-state demonstration.
Boundary / example: Use to resolve a specific uncertainty, not as a mandatory extra loop.

Definition for this course: Joint value and decision conversation with the customer sponsor and relevant owners.
Boundary / example: Stage 3 in referenced motion; sponsor/criteria/path decision.

Definition for this course: Positive Business Outcome: the beneficial business change the customer seeks.
Boundary / example: Not merely installing a product or holding a workshop.

Definition for this course: Source-aware point of view about problem, urgency, solution relevance and potential value to test.
Boundary / example: Not a measured result or guaranteed ROI.

Definition for this course: Why Change, Why Now and Why Glean.
Boundary / example: Customer-specific, linked to evidence and priority.

Definition for this course: A specific actor/job/trigger that may improve a business outcome.
Boundary / example: More concrete than improve support.

Definition for this course: Sequence of actors, steps, systems, inputs, handoffs, decisions and outputs.
Boundary / example: Map before proposing automation.

Definition for this course: How work happens today with evidence and uncertainty.
Boundary / example: Observed, interview-estimated or unknown must be labeled.

Definition for this course: Proposed changed workflow and retained controls/dependencies.
Boundary / example: Hypothesis until feasibility and outcome evidence support it.

Definition for this course: Business consequence and reach/frequency of an improvement.
Boundary / example: May involve cost, revenue, risk or quality; not seats alone.

Definition for this course: Technical, data, integration, security and organizational work required.
Boundary / example: Short user request can still imply high effort.

Definition for this course: High impact and low effort on the standard 2x2.
Boundary / example: Requires evidence; unknown feasibility is not automatically low effort.

Definition for this course: High-impact/high-effort use case.
Boundary / example: May be phased after readiness or a narrower first wave.

Definition for this course: Low-impact/low-effort use case.
Boundary / example: May be parked behind more relevant priorities.

Definition for this course: Low-impact/high-effort quadrant.
Boundary / example: Can be revisited if evidence or strategic priority changes.

Definition for this course: A small selected first-wave priority for deeper investigation.
Boundary / example: Sources vary on 3–4 versus 3–5; no universal exact-count rule here.

Definition for this course: Definition, units, cohort, baseline/target, source, owner, timing and caveats.
Boundary / example: Used to make success measurable and transferable.

Definition for this course: Agreed pre-change reference measurement for the defined cohort and period.
Boundary / example: A target or peer result is not the baseline.

Definition for this course: Pre-agreed measurable and quality conditions for evaluation/decision.
Boundary / example: Include owner, evidence and timing.

Definition for this course: Time a person spends doing the work.
Boundary / example: Distinct from elapsed waiting or total cycle duration.

Definition for this course: Wall-clock time from trigger to outcome, including waiting.
Boundary / example: Do not automatically monetize it as labor saved.

Definition for this course: Share of addressable users actively using the scoped workflow/tool.
Boundary / example: Separate from event frequency and recapture.

Definition for this course: Share of relevant content available/indexed/accessibly in scope.
Boundary / example: Method factor needs approved model interpretation; source formula ambiguity flagged.

Definition for this course: Share of raw avoidable burden that the solution could remove.
Boundary / example: Do not apply twice to already measured savings.

Definition for this course: Share of saved capacity deliberately converted into useful business output.
Boundary / example: Not user adoption or automatic cash saving.

Definition for this course: Equivalent value of freed/reallocated work capacity.
Boundary / example: Soft-dollar unless specific business/cost action establishes otherwise.

Definition for this course: Benefit tied to evidenced cost action, such as cancelled spend or a confirmed avoided cost.
Boundary / example: Requires actual cost scope and attribution; do not infer from salary-equivalent hours.

Definition for this course: A hypothesis supported by limited data or benchmarks with caveats.
Boundary / example: Pre-sale estimates should not be called realized value.

Definition for this course: Platform usage/engagement and related operational signals.
Boundary / example: Proves activity/adoption more directly than business attribution.

Definition for this course: Authoritative operational/financial source for a defined metric.
Boundary / example: Metric owner confirms definitions and access.

Definition for this course: Evidence that the intervention contributed to the observed business change.
Boundary / example: Before/after change alone may have confounders.

Definition for this course: Same-period benefit minus cost, divided by cost.
Boundary / example: Specify scope and benefit type; zero cost needs special handling.

Definition for this course: Illustrative time for modeled benefit to cover defined investment.
Boundary / example: ROI Lab is a simplified first-year benefit/cost illustration, not a full cash-flow model.

Definition for this course: Person with authority over the relevant investment decision.
Boundary / example: Not automatically the enthusiastic end user or technical champion.

Definition for this course: Customer advocate with influence, relevant engagement and a credible path to the decision process.
Boundary / example: Account team assesses evidence, not just enthusiasm.

Definition for this course: Business Value Consulting support for appropriately scoped value engagements.
Boundary / example: Internal routing/capacity and thresholds need current confirmation.

Definition for this course: Mutual Action Plan: customer-agreed milestones, owners, dependencies and decision checkpoints.
Boundary / example: Different from a seller-only private close plan.

Definition for this course: A curated/sample-data validation experience in the referenced material.
Boundary / example: Confirm current approved definition and limitations before offering.

Definition for this course: A temporary scoped environment whose current data/access/feature limitations must be confirmed.
Boundary / example: Not automatically a production-fidelity proof or universal entitlement.

Definition for this course: Separately justified and approved scoped evaluation tied to a buy/no-buy decision.
Boundary / example: Readiness score is evidence, not approval.

Definition for this course: Responsible, Accountable, Consulted and Informed responsibilities agreed for a task/decision.
Boundary / example: Course template does not override contractual or account ownership.

Definition for this course: LMS content/runtime packaging target used in the reference build notes.
Boundary / example: Actual runtime support must be tested in the intended Impartner tenant.

Definition for this course: Sharable Content Object launched and tracked by the LMS.
Boundary / example: Proposed architecture: one module per SCO ZIP plus separate final-exam ZIP.

Definition for this course: Minimum assessment score required to pass the configured learning object.
Boundary / example: 80 is supported by reference build; course-level aggregation is proposed.

Definition for this course: Permission/review decision for external or partner distribution of a claim or asset.
Boundary / example: Internal authoring access does not imply redistribution rights.

Definition for this course: Generated preparation material awaiting factual, technical and publication review.
Boundary / example: Never an automatic customer commitment or credential authority.
